answer.text: Feel the pain of losses approximately twice as intensely as the pleasure of equivalent gains, leading to irrational holding of losing investments
Never take any risk with their capital
Always sell winning investments too early

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XV (p.242), loss aversion is the tendency to strongly prefer avoiding losses to acquiring gains. The source states that the pain of loss is roughly twice as strong as the pleasure of a similar gain, and that holding on to losing stocks is a manifestation of this bias. The Trap: "Prefer losses over gains" inverts the concept. "Never take any risk" overstates loss aversion into total risk avoidance, which is not what the source describes. "Always sell winners too early" is a related but distinct disposition-effect symptom; the keyed answer captures the defining 2x asymmetry and the holding-losers behaviour the source uses to illustrate loss aversion. Note: The asymmetry — pain of loss roughly 2x pleasure of equivalent gain — is the load-bearing detail in the source's definition.
